name: cloud-c3
description: Diego's Cloud C3 - the fleet's command-and-control surface as its own APK, lifted out of the SuperApp's C3 section (#648). A five-tab shell drawn by the fleet's bottom-nav island (libs:bottomnav) - Topology, Observ, Home, Apps, Configs - declared in ui.* below and baked through BuildConfig. THE SHELL IS VIEWS AND HOSTS FRAGMENTS, not Compose: the pages this app exists to show are the SuperApp's C3 Fragments, and they are MOVED here rather than reauthored, so the rendering, wording and behaviour are the ones that already shipped. BottomNavIslandView is libs:bottomnav's own documented View-side contract for exactly this case (the SuperApp, cloud-me and cloud-wallet shells use it), so hosting fragments is a first-class path. Topology is the address estate: the SuperApp's c3_public and c3_private cards, one C3HealthFragment scoped two ways over the declared service tables. Observ is Health, the SuperApp's own page:c3/health. Home is the overview. Apps LAUNCHES the three C3 sibling APKs that already exist as their own fleet members through ui.external_apps, the same extapp: idiom the SuperApp used, so nothing is re-implemented; the printed name is DERIVED from each fleet id by dropping the family prefix, because an application has ONE name (#351). Configs holds About. A PAGE IS DECLARED WHEN ITS FRAGMENT EXISTS AND NOT BEFORE: there is no not-built body and no flag that could excuse one, which is what lets test/test-c3-shell.sh assert that every declared page renders real content - the guard whose absence let an empty five-tab APK ship green. The five feed cards, the ntfy centre and the three container dashboards ARRIVED (#648, owner-escalated): the ENTIRE SuperApp c3 section declaration is carried verbatim under ui.sections and its two stacks render as the Topology and Observability pages, with Dagu and the WG mesh as their own pages. The top offset is the MEASURED systemBars u displayCutout inset, read in a non-consuming listener (#407/#477), never a tuned margin. Dark is the default theme (#336, #337). English is the base language (#299). Build via Nix devShell, one APK out.

android._doc_application_id: The `c3-` / `cloud-` prefix is a DIRECTORY and fleet-name convention and is deliberately NOT in the applicationId — the ac_c3-watchtower precedent, whose own _doc records why: a wrong package compiles, ships, installs, and leaves a tab that opens nothing. `cloudc3` matches `clouddrive` / `cloudwallet`: the fleet name with its separator dropped.

signing._doc: ONE shared Cloud-constellation signing key for ALL Android apps. KEY LOCATION: A_A0-Providers/D_TOOLS-DEVICES/d2-android/release.jks (OU=Cloud Constellation) + A_A0-Providers/D_TOOLS-DEVICES/d2-android/signing.secrets.yaml.

modules._doc: Single source of truth for the Gradle module graph. settings.gradle iterates this list.

libs:core._doc_dir: Shared BY REFERENCE from ab_cloud-libs-shared/libs/ — settings.gradle points projectDir here instead of at a local copy, so a fix lands in every app at build time and copies cannot drift.

libs:devtools._doc_dir: Shared BY REFERENCE, same as libs:core. Not listed in app.depends_on and not linked in app/build.gradle: libs:core pulls it in with an `api` dependency, which is what gives every app the constellation-wide debug API (127.0.0.1:38090+, own-process logcat) without per-app wiring that would drift.

libs:updater._doc_dir: Shared BY REFERENCE from ab_cloud-libs-shared/libs/. Also the reader of the constellation fleet manifest: since #276's fix it falls back to aa_cloud-superapp/data/constellation-fleet.json when an app carries no data/ dir of its own, and throws if neither exists — which is why this app needs no data/ dir for the fleet bake.

libs:bottomnav._doc_dir: THE fleet bottom-nav island (#565/#579): the five tabs are drawn by the same Compose declaration superapp, mail, wallet, me and drive render — one geometry, one pill, one collapse rule. Shared BY REFERENCE like every other module here. This app reuses the four shared symbols (BottomNavEntry, BottomNavIsland, bottomNavInsets, rememberBottomNavCollapse) and declares its OWN five entries from ui.tabs; it deliberately does NOT reuse bottomnav's `bottomNavItems`, which is cloud-mail's item table and merely lives in that module.

libs:ops._doc_dir: Shared BY REFERENCE like every other module here. Carries DaguFragment (the native Dagu DAG list page:c3/dagu opens in the SuperApp) and DaguPrefs, the ONE store of the Authelia bearer the ops routes need. Its build.gradle reads THIS repository's build.json first (consumer-wins) for ui.sections[c3].pages[dagu].dagu_default_server, which is why the verbatim c3 section below is also the lib's config.

ui._doc: EVERY declarative list this app renders. app/build.gradle bakes each into BuildConfig as base64 JSON and Declarations.kt decodes it once; no screen reads a BuildConfig blob itself and no tab id, label or icon name is spelled in Kotlin.
ui._doc_tabs: #648 THE ONE tab declaration, in display order, Home deliberately the centre item the way every other fleet five-tab shell places it. Order is load-bearing: reordering this array reorders the bottom nav and nothing else changes, which is the property test/test-c3-shell.sh asserts. The ids are the ONLY tab ids in the app: C3Shell dispatches on them and the tester diffs that dispatch against this array in both directions, so a tab declared with no screen and a screen with no declared tab are both build failures.
ui._doc_c3_ops: The SAME c3-infra-api the SuperApp's C3 pages read (its build.json::ui.c3_ops). This APK is a new FRONT over the existing engine, not a second back end, so the base URL is declared once here and OpsClient is the only file that names a route.
ui._doc_external_apps: #648 THE APPS TAB. Watchdog, Morpheus and WatchTower are ALREADY standalone fleet members with their own directories, build.json, ship workflow and applicationId — so this tab LAUNCHES them and declares no page of its own. This is the same extapp: idiom the SuperApp's ui.sections[c3] used for exactly these three, moved here with the section. A tile resolves its package against the device rather than assuming it is installed, so a missing app reads as 'not installed' instead of a tap that does nothing.
ui._doc_external_apps_no_label: THERE IS NO `label` HERE, AND THAT IS THE #351/#224 RULE, not an omission. An application has ONE name — the fleet name in its own build.json::name — and a label sitting beside a package is a SECOND statement of it that drifts; #224 is literally the commit that reverted a display name back to the fleet name, and aa_cloud-superapp/test/test-app-names-pattern.sh T4 fails the build on any object that names one of our packages next to a disagreeing label. The id IS the name and is what the tile shows. The owner's request named these three as 'Watchdog', 'Morpheus' and 'Watchtower'; the fleet spells them c3-watchdog / c3-morpheus / c3-watchtower, and the spelling shown is the fleet's — reported to the owner rather than settled by adding a private display name here.

external_apps._doc: The phone's local web server (ac_cloud-c3-webserver, #687) is a cloud-c3 sub-app, so it launches from HERE beside the three siblings and not from the SuperApp's Cloud > Apps > Configs grid (aa_cloud-superapp/test/test-c3-family-apps.sh T2 fails if it goes back there). Still installed from the Store: its fleet row is untouched. No label (#351): the tile prints the id with the family prefix dropped.

ui._doc_pages: THE RULE (#648): a page appears here when its fragment exists, and not before. The SuperApp's five feed cards, its ntfy centre and its three container dashboards ARRIVED with the Observability/Topology stack pages above (C3StackFragment over ui.sections[c3].stack_*); Dagu and the WG mesh arrived as their own pages. The SuperApp page ids that have no fragment THERE either (reports, stack, workflows, vms, logs, gha — page_samples stubs) stay undeclared here, preserved only inside ui.sections[c3].pages; their More-row tiles dispatch an honest 'not shipped in this app'.

topology._doc: The address estate: the SuperApp's two c3_public / c3_private cards that sat under its Addresses heading. ONE fragment renders both, scoped — exactly how the SuperApp embedded it.

pages.label: Topology
pages._doc: #648 the SuperApp's Topology tab CARRIED WHOLE: C3StackFragment renders ui.sections[c3].stack_topology — Index tile row, the Addresses heading with the c3_public / c3_private cards, the Containers heading with the Infra Apps / User Apps dashboards, the Stack dashboard with its four declared anchors, and the More row. The sibling Public/Private pages below stay: they are the same two cards standalone, exactly as this app already shipped them, and nothing is deleted in a copy job.

observ._doc: What the estate is doing. Today that is Health — the SuperApp's own page:c3/health, both tables with their counts in one view.

pages.label: Observability
pages._doc: #648 the SuperApp's Observability tab CARRIED WHOLE: C3StackFragment renders ui.sections[c3].stack_observability — the Index row, the FIVE feed cards (Analytics/github_run_stats, GHA/github_runs, Dagu/dagu_runs, GH Repos/github_commits, Gitea Repos/gitea_commits), the NTFY notification centre (stream=channels, last 5 per channel), and the More row.

pages.label: Dagu
pages._doc: #648 the SuperApp's page:c3/dagu — libs:ops DaguFragment, the native DAG list with per-row Run buttons and the Authelia-bearer login whose server URL pre-fills from ui.sections[c3].pages[dagu].dagu_default_server. The same fragment the Dagu feed card's rows and the More row target.

pages.label: WG mesh
pages._doc: #648 the SuperApp's page:wg/status — C3MeshFragment over the canonical wg-mesh/v1 snapshot (data/mesh.json), grouped by transport. It is the More row's 'WG mesh' target on the Observability stack, which is why it lives under this tab.

configs._doc: This app's own settings. About is real because everything it shows is baked by gradle; a General page arrives when it has something to set.

ui._doc_icons: An icon name here is a DRAWABLE name in res/drawable, resolved by getIdentifier at runtime (the ac_cloud-me contract). It is no longer a Compose vocabulary key: the shell is Views, because the pages this app hosts are the Fragments the SuperApp already had. A name with no drawable resolves to 0 and draws a blank square, so test-c3-shell.sh asserts every declared name has a file and every file is declared — in both directions.
ui._doc_tile_columns: How many tiles an index/dashboard row holds before wrapping — the SAME value the SuperApp bakes (ui.tile_columns), moved with the stacks that read it (IndexTiles.grid, the cloud_dashboard icon grids).
ui._doc_sections: #648 THE ENTIRE c3 declaration block of aa_cloud-superapp/build.json::ui.sections[id=c3], carried over VERBATIM — tabs, the visible AND hidden pages, stack_observability (the five feed cards + the NTFY centre + the Index/More rows) and stack_topology (the address cards + the three container dashboards), every _doc intact. THIS COPY IS WHAT THE APP RENDERS: app/build.gradle bakes stack_observability / stack_topology from HERE, and libs:ops reads pages[dagu].dagu_default_server from HERE (its consumer-wins lookup is ui.sections[id=c3]). The SuperApp's own copy stays where it was; this one is the independently editable duplicate the fleet's COPY rule asks for. Page ids that carry no fragment in the SuperApp either (reports, stack, workflows, vms, logs, gha land on its page_samples stub) are NOT declared as pages of this app's tabs — the #648 rule stands: a page is declared when its fragment exists — but their declarations are preserved here and their tiles in the two stacks dispatch an honest 'not shipped in this app' rather than a dead tap.

sections.label: C3
sections._doc_parent: Back from the C3 tab strip ROOT lands on Cloud, not Home. navigateUpToParent() consults parent only when the back stack is empty, which is exactly the strip-root case — without this, that press fell through to goHome(). Distinct from the tab-restore fix in LauncherNavController (activeTabBySection), which governs returning from a SUBPAGE to the tab it was opened from.
sections._doc_tabs: C3 IS its two halves, so it wears the same tab strip every other tabbed section wears (SectionTabsFragment + AppTabsStyle, driven purely by `tabs` + the visible `pages` below). Observability and Topology are the only two listed pages; the six detail pages under them are `hidden` — still routable as page:c3/<id>, and reached from the tile_row that leads each tab, exactly where they were reached from before. Two listed pages is also what makes this a strip rather than a rail: goSection only falls to SectionMenuFragment past SectionTabsFragment.MAX_PANES.

pages.label: Topology
pages._doc: What the cloud IS — the container/stack dashboard that used to be the whole of Cloud ▸ C3, carried down one level unchanged. Reports are NOT here any more: they are output rather than structure, so the reports tile now lives in stack_observability. page:c3/reports itself is unchanged and still routes the same way. FIRST tab: structure before behaviour, and it is also the landing page, because SectionTabsFragment.startIndex falls to the first page with a blank `action`. The `|` divider is unaffected — it is positioned by indexOfFirst { action.isNotBlank() }, which is still Watchdog at index 2 whichever way the two content tabs are ordered.

pages.label: Observability
pages._doc: What the cloud is DOING — GHA + Dagu workflow runs, the full Dagu workflow inventory, the reports the cloud produces, the workflow pages, and per-repo commit history. Reports moved here from Topology: Topology is what the fleet IS, and a report is output, not structure. A facet renders this section's own stack_observability; `facet` needs no `is_aggregator` on the section, only a stack_<page id> to read.

pages.label: Watchdog
pages._doc: A LAUNCH tab, not a content tab: it carries no facet and no fragment, only the same `action` grammar Configs' Keyboard entry uses, so tapping it dispatches extapp:c3-watchdog and the C3 strip stays where it was. That reuses launchExternalApp verbatim — the app opens when com.diegonmarcos.watchdog is installed, and when it is NOT the user is told so and the APK from ui.external_apps[id=c3-watchdog].install_apk_url is offered, instead of a tab that does nothing. is_action is what stops it being counted as a page anywhere a page means content.

pages.label: Morpheus
pages._doc: The second LAUNCH tab, identical in shape to Watchdog above: dispatches extapp:c3-morpheus (com.diegonmarcos.morpheus), falling back to installing ui.external_apps[id=c3-morpheus].install_apk_url. Morpheus shipped recently, so the not-installed path is the COMMON one here, not the edge case.

pages.label: WatchTower
pages._doc: The third LAUNCH tab, identical in shape to Watchdog and Morpheus above: no facet, no fragment, only an `action`, so tapping it dispatches extapp:c3-watchtower (com.diegonmarcos.watchtower) and the C3 strip stays where it was. Not installed -> the user is told so and ui.external_apps[id=c3-watchtower].install_apk_url is offered. is_action is what stops it being counted as a page anywhere a page means content. THE APP IS BRAND NEW, so the not-installed path is the ONLY path until the first ship run publishes, exactly as Morpheus's _doc records of its own first days.
pages._doc_index: INDEX 4, AFTER MORPHEUS, and the position is the requirement rather than a detail of it - the owner asked for it 'beside Morpheus'. It is also what leaves the `|` divider alone: SectionTabsFragment positions the divider with indexOfFirst { action.isNotBlank() }, which is Watchdog at index 2 both before and after this insertion. Inserting anywhere BEFORE index 2 would move the divider and silently restructure the whole strip. test/test-watchtower-tab.sh asserts the index and the divider, not merely that the tab exists.
pages._doc_icon: ic_p_c3_reports - the page-family icon for output rather than structure, which is what an analytics read is. Deliberately NOT a new drawable: Sections.iconResFor falls back to ic_link_tile IN SILENCE when a name resolves to nothing, so an invented name would render as a generic link with no error anywhere.

pages.label: Dagu
pages._doc: Target of the `Dagu events` tile and of the Infra RSS stack's `Dagu · Workflow runs` link. SectionPages routes c3/dagu to OpsPages.fragmentForDagu() (the native DAG list), but the page was undeclared, so both entry points landed on the C3 section instead. hidden: it is reached by tile, not from the section's child list.

pages.label: GHA
pages._doc: Target of the `GHA events` tile. Declared so the target resolves and the tile lands on PageContentFragment's stub, which is what an un-wired page is supposed to do here. There is NO native fragment yet — libs:ops OpsPages says as much ('future "gha" once that lands'); until it does, this is a placeholder, not a working screen.

stack_observability._doc: INDEX of this page, same contract as stack_topology's: every tile is an `anchor:` id resolved by StackAnchors against the cards below, so the row is a table of contents rather than a set of deep links. One tile per card (Analytics, GHA, Dagu, GH Repos, Gitea Repos, NTFY), in the same order the cards render below. A CARD ADDED BELOW WITHOUT A TILE HERE IS HALF A CHANGE: that is what task #78 ('add top Index card, fix broken+duplicated More row') fixed, so leaving the Analytics card out of this row would have been #78 regressing on the same page it was fixed on.
stack_observability.title: Index
stack_observability.subtitle: Jump to a card on this page

stack_observability._doc:
ANALYTICS — the glance. Every other card on this page is a FEED: the latest N things that happened. This one is the only card that counts rather than lists, and that is exactly what the owner asked WatchTower to be, stated at card depth: over the last `limit` runs per repo, how many ran, what share of the FINISHED ones went green, and how long ago the last green was.

WHY THE DENOMINATOR IS 'FINISHED' AND NOT 'ALL'. A run still in progress carries an empty `conclusion`. Counting those as not-green makes the rate sag every time the fleet is mid-build, which is precisely when somebody opens this page. Queued and running are neither green nor failed — they are not yet anything. renderRunStatsFeed divides by the finished count and says 'no verdicts yet' rather than '0%' when that count is zero, because a rate with an empty denominator is not a rate.

SOURCE, NOT A NEW KIND. kind=feed with a sixth `source`, per this page's own long-standing instruction: a new integration is a new `when` arm in AggregatorStackFragment.renderFeed plus a client, never a new panel `kind`. It reads the SAME GitHubFeed.runs() the GHA card above reads, through the same 15-minute cache, so the two cards cost ONE fetch per repo between them and cannot disagree about a number.

THE REPO SET IS THIS ARRAY AND NOTHING ELSE, the same contract the GH Repos card documents. Deliberately the same three as the GHA card below (android/cloud/front) rather than ac_c3-watchtower's five: this is the glance and stays narrow, the app is the detail and carries the wider set. Adding a repo here is a data edit, never a Kotlin one.

OPENING THE FULL THING: the card's summary row targets extapp:c3-watchtower, so a tap hands off to the app through the SAME single dispatch chokepoint every other row uses (onTileClicked -> routeTarget -> launchExternalApp) — no seventh ad-hoc ACTION_VIEW site (#156), and the click still fires exactly once (#195). It is NOT in the More row below: More opens 'the full page behind a card' and its tiles are ordinary page: targets into HIDDEN c3 pages. There is no page:c3/analytics, and inventing one to have somewhere to point would add an un-wired stub page to satisfy a row.
stack_observability.title: Analytics
stack_observability.subtitle: Delivery over the last 30 runs per repo · green rate, failures, last green

stack_observability.title: GHA
stack_observability.subtitle: Last 5 GitHub Actions workflow runs · cloud + front family

stack_observability._doc: Last 5 Dagu runs across EVERY registered DAG, most-recent-first — a real run HISTORY, not the old dagu_dags kind's one-row-per-DAG registry (that showed each DAG's latest run only; this can show the same DAG twice if it ran twice in the top 5). Backed by GET /api/v1/dag-runs?limit=5 (DaguRunsFeed.kt, aa_cloud-superapp-only per this task's scope — NOT a change to ab_cloud-libs-shared's DaguClient), confirmed live 2026-09-06 to already answer newest-first with `limit` honored server-side. c3-infra-api's own /workflows/dagu proxy is unrelated and unused here — this card, like the native page:c3/dagu list, talks to Dagu directly via DaguPrefs so there is one Dagu config on the device.
stack_observability.title: Dagu
stack_observability.subtitle: Last 5 Dagu workflow runs · status

stack_observability._doc: Last COMMIT per repo (limit=1, not the old 'latest 3') from the whole cloud + front family. THIS ARRAY IS THE REPO SET: AggregatorStackFragment.renderRepoCommitsFeed iterates Sections.StackPanel.repos and nothing else, so adding a repo is a data edit here, never a Kotlin edit. The list is every repo of the two families that GitHub actually answers 200 for, verified against api.github.com/repos/diegonmarcos/<name>. DELIBERATELY EXCLUDED, so nobody re-adds them: `cloud-android` and `cloud-unix` answer 301 and redirect to `cloud-u-android` and `cloud-infra-desktop` respectively — they are rename-aliases of repos already listed, and adding them would duplicate every commit; `cloud-mykonsole-dtk` answers 404, the upstream is gone and only the gitea mirror still remembers it; `front` (the ~30-project web monorepo) answers 404 too — it has no GitHub remote at all, and diegonmarcos.github.io is the published front site, which is why THAT is the front entry rather than `front`. Rate limit: this panel plus GHA share GitHub's 60-requests-per-hour anonymous quota, so GitHubFeed caches for 15 minutes, staggers the fan-out, and reports an exhausted quota as `rate limited` rather than as an empty repo. This SAME repo list (different `owner`) is reused verbatim by the Gitea Repos card below, so the two cards are directly comparable — same repos, two mirrors.
stack_observability.title: GH Repos
stack_observability.subtitle: Last commit per repo · cloud + front family

stack_observability._doc: Same 8 repos as GH Repos, one mirror over. `owner` is `diego` (infra-dat_gitea's org — see cloud-u-containers/infra-dat_gitea/src/build.json::gitea.org) rather than `diegonmarcos`: GiteaFeed.kt hits http://10.0.0.6:3002/api/v1/repos/diego/<repo>/commits directly (mesh-only, confirmed live and unauthenticated for these public mirrors — 10.0.0.x is already cleartext-allowed in network_security_config.xml), NOT the public git.diegonmarcos.com domain, which sits behind two-factor auth this app cannot complete. Gitea mirrors EVERY non-fork GitHub repo except cloud-vault (mirror_policy.exclude), a much longer list than these 8 — this card deliberately reuses the SAME curated family as GH Repos rather than all ~30+ mirrors, so the two cards read as 'the same repos, two remotes' instead of one card being a long unrelated scroll.
stack_observability.title: Gitea Repos
stack_observability.subtitle: Last commit per repo · gitea mirror

stack_observability._doc: Last 5 messages per channel, EVERY ntfy channel in one card — replacing the old three scope-split cards (Advisories/My channels/Cloud channels). No `scopes` declared: renderNtfyGroups already treats an empty scopes list as 'every channel', so simply not filtering is the whole change, not a new code path. `limit: 5` caps rows per channel group (paintNtfyGroup), separate from the Inboxes ▸ C3 Ntfy card below which reuses the exact same kind/stream unbounded. Channel list is resolved from ui.ntfy (this build.json's own mirror of cloud-u-containers/infra-obs_ntfy/src/build.json::topics[] — see _doc_ntfy) through NtfyScopes, so a channel added upstream appears here on the next build with no second list to edit.
stack_observability.title: NTFY
stack_observability.subtitle: Last 5 messages per channel · every channel

stack_observability._doc: MORE — the full pages behind this tab's cards, plus (as of the five-feed-card rework) the two pages that lost their only referrer when Inboxes ▸ C3 Ntfy stopped being a signpost: `health` and `wg-mesh` below point at page:c3/health and page:wg/status, both HIDDEN pages that tile_row used to be the sole way into. Ordinary `page:` targets, no anchor grammar: this opens the PAGE, which carries what a card cannot (DaguFragment lists AND starts runs, the log viewer is per-VM, C3 health has its own scope-filtered view). Subordinate by position — it sits at the bottom, after the five feed cards — so the cards stay the first thing read. Dropping any tile here without giving its target page another referrer fails test/test-stack-anchors-declared.sh's T8.
stack_observability.title: More
stack_observability.subtitle: Open the full page behind a card

stack_topology._doc: INDEX of this page, not a set of deep links. Every tile is an `anchor:` target handled by StackAnchors inside AggregatorStackFragment: it scrolls this stack to the card that claimed the id, so the row is a table of contents for what is already below it rather than four ways to leave. The four `stack/*` ids address SUB-TABLES of the single `cloud_dashboard` Stack card — that card renders groups providers/dbs/mcpapi from data/cloud_services.json, and the group and subgroup headers it draws register their own anchors, so Providers · VMs · Dbs · APIs are addressable WITHOUT splitting one card into four panels the data does not have (VMs and Runners are both subgroups of `providers`; APIs and MCPs are both subgroups of `mcpapi`). WG mesh left this row: the WireGuard screen is Configs ▸ WireGuard (page:config/wg → WireGuardFragment) and does not need a second entry point here. Drive · Connections left it too and now lives under Cloud ▸ Apps ▸ Data Apps, pointing at the same page:drive/connections.
stack_topology.title: Index
stack_topology.subtitle: Jump to a table on this page

stack_topology._doc: Heading over the two URL cards, so the Public/Private pair reads as one titled block the way 'Containers' and 'Stack' already do below. Same section_title kind — a plain heading between cards, not a card.
stack_topology.title: Addresses

stack_topology._doc: Routed URLs — what the fleet EXPOSES and where each name actually goes. Data-driven from data/services_public.json (43 rows), the same regen.sh snapshot the C3 Health page reads, so nothing is hand-listed here and nothing can rot out of step with the infra: the panel kind c3_public already renders exactly the wanted shape (name · auth · https://<public_url> · 🔒 <private_dns, which is host:port> · vm). TITLE SAYS 'routes', deliberately, NOT 'internet-reachable': services_public.json means A PROXY ROUTE EXISTS, and regen.sh never reads wg_only — eight sibling MCPs are wg_only:true yet appear here on mcp.diegonmarcos.com routes, mesh-gated with a 403 fallback. Claiming those are public would make this card assert something false about the security posture, which is worse than not having the card; per-row wg_only would be truer still, but it is not in the snapshot and inventing it here rather than in regen.sh is exactly the rot this file avoids.
stack_topology.title: Public URLs · proxy routes
stack_topology.subtitle: public host → upstream host:port · a route exists, not necessarily open to the internet

stack_topology._doc: The other half: containers with NO proxy route at all — reachable only over the WireGuard mesh. Data-driven from data/services_private.json (60 rows) via the existing c3_private panel kind (name · protocol/db · service · 🔒 <private_dns, host:port> · vm). Together with the card above this answers 'what is exposed and where does it actually go' from ONE generated source rather than from either Caddyfile — which matters because there are two of them (infra-sec_caddy on gcp-proxy = mesh side, infra-sec_caddy-public on oci-analytics = public edge) and because the public edge's repo dist is NOT what is deployed.
stack_topology.title: Private URLs · mesh only
stack_topology.subtitle: no proxy route — WireGuard host:port

stack_topology._doc: Cloud dashboard — section_title dividers + 3 collapsible cloud_dashboard CARDS. 'Containers' heading → Infra Apps + User Apps (every container exactly once). 'Stack' heading → the Stack card (free cross-cut lists: Providers/VMs · DBs · MCP & API). Grouping + inventory DATA-DRIVEN from data/cloud_services.json (BuildConfig.CLOUD_SERVICES_B64), generated by data/gen_cloud_services.js from cloud/a_solutions. renderCloudDashboard draws an icon grid (ui.tile_columns/line) with a STATUS LIGHT under each icon (TCP-ping over WireGuard) + opens the URL in the in-app browser on tap. `group`/`groups` selects which cloud_services.json group(s) a card renders.
stack_topology.title: Containers
Stack
stack_topology._doc_anchors: The sub-tables this ONE card provides as anchor targets, declared the way a section declares its pages: an `id` other tiles point at with `target: "anchor:<id>"`, plus the header inside this card it lands on. `group` alone binds to that group's header; adding `subgroup` binds to a sub-header under it. The id is NEVER derived from a label — renaming the "VMs" sub-header cannot rename `stack/vms`, it only breaks the binding, and test/test-stack-anchors-declared.sh fails on a binding whose group/subgroup is not in data/cloud_services.json. It also removes the old ambiguity where group "DBs (storage)" and subgroup "DBs" both slugged to `dbs`: `stack/dbs` says group, so it lands on the group header by declaration rather than by registration order.

stack_topology._doc: MORE — the same contract as Observability's row: ordinary `page:` targets to the full pages, sitting below everything the Index indexes so the table of contents is still read first. These two had no referrer anywhere in build.json once the Index became pure anchors. The distinction is real and not redundancy: `anchor:stack/vms` scrolls to the VMs sub-table inside the Stack card, while `page:c3/vms` opens the VMs PAGE, which carries per-VM detail the card's icon grid does not.

ui._doc_ntfy:
USER vs INFRA channel split for the ntfy registry. The channels are one flat list of snake_case topics upstream, so 'my notifications' and 'the cloud's notifications' arrived indistinguishable in one alphabetical wall. Scope is decided by the topic PREFIX, declared here rather than hardcoded in the fragment (FIRE RULE #6): a new prefix is a build.json edit. Anything unmatched counts as INFRA, so a channel can never silently vanish from the list — it lands in the cloud bucket and is visible enough to classify.

`channels` below IS the ntfy registry's own topics[] list — the source of truth is /home/appuser/git/cloud-u-containers/infra-obs_ntfy/src/build.json::topics (this app's clone lives at cloud-u-android, a SIBLING checkout to cloud-u-containers, not a `a_solutions` submodule of it — a path this comment previously got wrong). Verified 2026-09-06: every one of that registry's 23 topic names is present below; `cloud-sa-notifications` / `fleet_advisory` / `infra_mail-health` are the only extras, and they are legitimately NOT in that registry — they are this app's own advisory-scope channels (see `advisory_topic` below), published by a different mechanism than the fleet's ntfy topic list. There is no automated sync from that JSON into this one yet (the two live in different repos and this task's scope did not include building that pipeline); a topic added to the registry needs a matching manual edit here until one exists.
ui._doc_ntfy_copy: #648 VERBATIM copy of the SuperApp's ui.ntfy (labels, scopes, taxon, channels, poll origin) — the catalog the NTFY card in stack_observability resolves its channel list, labels and poll URL from (NtfyCatalog/NtfyScopes, moved with the card).

ntfy._doc_base_url: Origin for PROGRAMMATIC reads (the JSON poll API). This is ntfy itself on the WireGuard mesh. It is NOT rss.diegonmarcos.com: that hostname is the same container behind Caddy, whose only anonymous prefix is /feed* (infra-sec_caddy/src/caddyfile.nix::mkNtfyBlock, feed_auth="none"), and /feed* is served by the rss-gateway sidecar which publishes profiles.json, channels.json and <profile>.atom / c/<topic>.atom — it has no /<topic>/json route at all. Every other path on that host falls through to `handle { forward_auth authelia }` and answers 302 to the SSO portal, which is the 401 the Notify cards rendered. Measured anonymously from a mesh peer on 2026-09-09: /feed/channels.json 200, /feed/<topic>/json 404, /<topic>/json 302 -> auth.diegonmarcos.com, http://10.0.0.6:8090/<topic>/json 200 for all 26 channels below.
ntfy._doc_web_base_url: Origin for HUMAN links — the topic page a card opens in the in-app browser. The public hostname on purpose: a WebView carries the Authelia session cookie and satisfies the gate, which is the tier that exists for people.
ntfy._doc_poll_window: `since` for the channel cards, in a unit ntfy parses — s/m/h, a Unix timestamp, a message id or `all`. NEVER `d`: since=7d answers HTTP 400 {"code":40008}. Kept at a day rather than a week because health_resources alone replays 851 KB / 2101 messages over 24h and 3.6 MB over 168h, and a shade only ever shows the newest handful.

ntfy._doc_labels: Human titles, loosely mirrored from the fleet's own registry at cloud-u-containers/infra-obs_ntfy/src/build.json::topics[].desc (the source of truth) — reworded for length rather than copied verbatim. A raw snake_case topic is an address, not a name: 'sec_yara' tells you nothing about what arrives there, and a list of twenty-six of them is an inventory nobody reads. A topic with no entry here still renders — under its raw name — because a missing label must degrade to less readable, never to invisible.

ntfy._doc_taxon: Section PREFIX per cloud publisher, in the same one-character vocabulary ui.phone_sections declares ("_" Sys, "@" Inboxes & AI, "." Data Apps, "=" Primary, ">" Media, "*" Health, "-"/"+" Services). The Notify tabs narrow phone groups by running PhoneAppClassifier over each package, but a cloud message carries no package — only an ntfy topic or an in-app producer name — so there is nothing to classify and this map is the classification. Without it every cloud publisher passed the taxonomy filter untouched and the SuperApp updater appeared on all six tabs, listed under Inboxes and under Data Apps as readily as under Sys. A key that is NOT declared here shows on the All tab only: a publisher nobody has categorised must not silently claim a category. Keys are matched against the group key, which is the topic for a channel and NotificationStore.source for the in-app feed.

tests._doc: Read by 1_cicd/dist/scripts/cloud-android-test-engine.sh, which the ship workflow runs before it builds.

shell._doc_requires: A tester that shells out to a tool which is not installed does not fail — it returns a verdict from the tool's ABSENCE. Listing them here makes a missing one fatal at the engine's preflight instead of a green tick over assertions that never ran.

unit._doc: Runs gradle test (build.sh test) on every ship. app/src/test carries the declaration parser's JVM suite, which exercises the SAME parser the phone runs against this repository's own build.json.
